brief: A wall clock with hands that turn and tell the time.

requirements.requirement: Wall clock with hands that turn and tell time
requirements.evidence: No clock mechanism, motor, pivot or moving hands exist in the parts catalog (find_parts/props for 'clock' returned 0). Current build is 7x full hex bases (piece:0,0,0;full + 6 neighbors) with 7x top covers forming a clock-like face and one pencil prop (prop:3) - static only, no rotation, no timekeeping. 3D-printed plastic parts cannot provide accurate timekeeping (configurator checks fit only).

finish.summary: Build is a 7-cell hex cluster with solid top covers as a clock-face plaque plus wall keyhole mount. No moving/accurate clock function is possible in Hex Cluster - no mechanism parts exist.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text:
The build is a 7-cell hexagonal cluster (central + 6 around) with solid top covers forming a large ~450mm clock-like face and a keyhole accessory for wall hanging. What was requested cannot be provided in this system:

* No clock mechanism exists in the catalog — `find_parts` / `find_props` for "clock" returns nothing. There is no motor, hands pivot, gear, or timekeeping part.
* No part allows continuous rotation or accurate timekeeping. The configurator only checks 3D-printed plastic fit, not electronics, strength or time accuracy.
* The attempted staging with pencil/pen as hands was removed/failed to place reliably and would in any case be static props, not turning hands.

The current build is only a decorative circular wall plaque that *suggests* a clock face, not a working clock.
